summary: This is a reference page for the OCTET_LENGTH function, which returns the length of a string or binary value in bytes. For ASCII strings the result equals LENGTH, while for strings containing Unicode code points it is greater than LENGTH; for binary values it always equals LENGTH. The page gives the syntax, a single argument description, and an example query showing results for a 3-character ASCII string, a Greek capital beta character, and a binary literal.
one_line: Reference for the OCTET_LENGTH function, which returns the byte length of a string or binary value.
key_facts: OCTET_LENGTH returns the length of a string or binary value in bytes.
For ASCII strings, OCTET_LENGTH is the same as LENGTH.
For strings using Unicode code points, OCTET_LENGTH is greater than LENGTH.
For binary values, OCTET_LENGTH is always the same as LENGTH.
The single argument is string_or_binary, the string or binary value for which the length is returned.
The examples are shown in a single SELECT statement with three result columns.
The page lists the function under categories including Encoding/Decoding and String Manipulation-related groups such as General Manipulation and Case Conversion.
